Emma — attaching the summarized test results (perf-results-hosted.csv and perf-summary-private.pdf). Key findings and recommendations below.

Summary (selected highlights):
- Hosted baseline (open-llm-medium): short prompts (<=32 tokens) P95 = 480ms at 8 concurrent sessions; throughput ~4.2k tokens/sec sustained. TTFT median 85ms. Variance increases above 16 concurrent sessions (P95 up to 820ms).
- Dedicated (reserved pool, quantized medium): short prompts P95 = 320ms at 16 concurrent sessions; throughput ~9.5k tokens/sec. Isolation tests show <6% variance P95 across noisy tenant runs. Autoscale ramp-to-steady achieved in ~75s after spike.
- Private pilot (customer infra, identical instance type): P95 = 360ms at 16 concurrent sessions; throughput ~8.7k tokens/sec. Observed a couple of TTFT spikes correlated with kube-scheduler pod churn (we captured node events). After tuning kubelet eviction thresholds and pinning NUMA policy, spikes reduced and parity improved to ~10% delta vs Dedicated.

Interpretation and recommendation:
- For immediate go-live (production-facing feature) we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) to hit predictable latency targets and minimize variance during scale events.
- Hosted is acceptable for initial rollout and lower concurrency workloads but will need caching/quotas for predictable SLAs.
- Private can reach parity but requires infra tuning and a small runbook (included in perf-summary-private.pdf).

Proposed MAP adjustments (timeline):
- 11/11 — finalize Dedicated sizing and pricing (sales tick: reserve 4x r8g-8 units)
- 11/18 — internal PO approval and legal review for Dedicated contract
- 11/24 — procurement sign-off (target)
- 12/06 — Dedicated pool live for customer (onboarding window)

Attachments: perf-results-hosted.csv (raw runs), perf-summary-private.pdf (private pilot narrative & runbook).

Let me know if you want an executive one-pager — I can prep for your CFO.
